newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says cannot confirm Iraq missile report.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says cannot confirm Iraq missile report.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Sunday he could not confirm sketchy reports that Iraq may have fired more antiaircraft missiles at U.S. and allied aircraft patrolling a "no-fly" zone over southern Iraq.

Speaking to reporters before boarding his helicopter on a campaign trip to Iowa, Clinton said, "I can't confirm that", when asked about a report attributed by a wire service to Defense Secretary William Perry. Separately, a senior White House official said the statement purportedly made by Perry was "a false report."
The official said there was no indication Iraq had taken any new aggressive or offensive military moves in the Gulf.
Samuel Berger, Clinton's deputy national security adviser, discounted the remark attributed to Perry as a "garbled report."
He said he believed any such comments by Perry referred to the Iraqi missile firings earlier in the week that prompted a U.S. buildup for possible renewed U.S. punitive strikes.
"We have no reports here of firings in the last day," Berger said on the CNN program "Late Edition."
